subject: Linguistics
title: Literacy and Power
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Literacy and Power.

hook.text: In ancient Egypt, only scribes could read—literacy was a monopoly that sustained the pharaoh's power.

buildup.text: Throughout history, controlling literacy meant controlling information, law, and religion.

discovery.text: The alphabet's simplicity democratized reading—fewer symbols meant more people could learn.

twist.text: Even today, 770 million adults can't read—literacy remains unevenly distributed worldwide.

climax.text: Writing systems shape who gets access to knowledge—and who gets excluded.

punchline.text: Who can read decides who has power.

quiz.question: How did simpler alphabets affect literacy?
options: They made reading accessible to more people
